_read_this_first: The queue row is spelled `OneUpMushroom`. That is a COINED project name and it is NOT in the cartridge.
The cartridge's own RTTI name for this class is `da1up_c`. Write the class as `da1up_c`.
This file is named after the queue row so the writer can find it from `tu-promotion-queue.tsv`; `class` below is the real identity.

Read directly out of extracted/dsd/arm9_overlays/ov002.bin, not from build/rtti.json (rtti.json agrees). The strict length-prefixed search for `13OneUpMushroom\0` returns ABSENT from every image.

pointer_to_member_table._why_this_matters: This is the structural heart of the class and the single biggest thing the writer must not discover by accident: da1up_c is a 14-state machine dispatched through an array of pointers-to-member, and 14 of the 27 unnamed members are its states.
pointer_to_member_table.bss_extent_evidence: The next bss symbol in ov002 is at 0x0210dc70, so the array is exactly 0x70 = 14 * 8 bytes. The sinit's last store is `str r3, [r5, #0x6c]`, which writes the 14th record's second word.
pointer_to_member_table.alignment_proof: 14 relocations, kind:load, at an exact 8-byte stride beginning at 0x02108300, each pointing at a function inside this run; the second word of every record is 0x00000000 (zero `this` adjustment). Reading the band 4 bytes off would place zero relocations on the record-start words, so the alignment is settled by the relocation stride itself, not by eyeballing.
pointer_to_member_table.consumer: _ZN13OneUpMushroom8BehaviorEv (0x020b00e8..0x020b01c0) is the ONLY reader of 0x0210dc00 anywhere in the ROM besides the sinit itself. That one-consumer-inside-the-TU shape is exactly how notes/sinit-ownership-pilot-ov002.md established dEnemyBase_c's two PMF tables.
pointer_to_member_table.ownership: This TU owns the array, the 14 descriptors and the sinit. notes/sinit-ownership-pilot-ov002.md independently resolves __sinit_ov002_02100adc to `ov002/OneUpMushroom` high-confidence, and records the organic compiler proof: under pinned mwccarm 2004/b56 a non-const file-scope PMF array emits exactly one .init function, one 4-byte .ctor entry, and N separate 8-byte .data descriptors each with one R_ARM_ABS32 at offset 0 and a zero adjustment. That is byte-for-byte the shape measured here.
pointer_to_member_table.index_map_evidence: Derived twice, independently, and the two agree exactly. (1) By hand, tracing register dataflow through the sinit's disassembly: each `ldr rX,[pc,#N]` literal resolves to a descriptor address, `ldr [rX]` / `ldr [rX,#4]` fetch the pair, and the `str [r5,#8*i]` / `str [r5,#8*i+4]` pair names the index. (2) The existing shard src/__sinit_ov002_02100adc.c already expresses the same 14 assignments. All 14 descriptors are used exactly once and all 14 targets are distinct.
pointer_to_member_table.member_ness_is_proven: A pointer-to-member-function descriptor can only designate a non-static member function, and every adjustment word here is 0, so all 14 are members of da1up_c with `this` at offset 0. Their INDEX in the table is also ROM-proven. Only the NAME of each is unknown.

blockers.title: Renaming any of the 14 PMF members without moving its symbols.txt row in the SAME commit links that descriptor as 0x00000000.
blockers.detail: The 14 descriptors at 0x02108300..0x02108370 sit in UNOWNED .data as `data_ov002_*` rows, and dsd resolves those records by SYMBOL NAME. Every one currently spells its target `func_ov002_*`. No byte gate at stage 2 or 3 catches a silently-zeroed descriptor. This is the exact hazard the pipeline warns about, and this class has 14 instances of it.

blockers.title: `promotion_route: text-only` is not the whole story -- this TU owns a static initializer.
blockers.detail: Unlike the daBar_c oracle, this TU emits a .init function (__sinit_ov002_02100adc, 0x174 bytes), a 4-byte .ctor entry at 0x021080d8, 14 .data PMF descriptors, and a 0x70-byte .bss array. If the writer declares the PMF array in the TU, mwccarm will generate all of that (notes/sinit-ownership-pilot-ov002.md proves the shape reproduces organically under the pinned compiler); it then has to be handled as compiler-only output, and the sinit is CODE, so it is not a plain `deadstrip-data` row like daBar_c's ten. If the writer instead leaves the array extern, Behavior() keeps loading someone else's symbol and the 14 states never become members. Decide this deliberately, and note that `src/__sinit_ov002_02100adc.c` is a 39th shard outside the 36 the queue counts.
